result: PASS BIOS boot with qemu64; full lifecycle tracked separately
scope: Local final ISO boot; raw logs remain private ignored files.
observations: Default q35/TCG multi-thread boot repeatedly panicked during IO-APIC timer initialization before appliance init.
Same default VM launch of the unchanged 0.7 ISO reproduced the same kernel panic; both releases use the same kernel hash.
Single-thread TCG, pc machine, increased RAM/CPU, quiet kernel probe and hpet-off probes did not independently resolve the panic.

q35/TCG single-thread with icount shift=auto,align=off,sleep=on passed kernel initialization and reached ROUTERTOP_READY at 256 MiB/2 vCPUs. Initial first-boot DHCP acquisition needed a longer bounded wait.
Final ISO and kernel arguments were not changed. Temporary lab DHCP helper was stopped and its primary interface IPv4 address removed before PPP/IPv6 actual browser acceptance.

Controlled retry with packet builder idle still reproduced the default multi-thread TCG timer panic. RC2 fresh ISO BIOS boot and initial API200 setup-required passed with the recorded icount settings; complete lifecycle is reported separately.

Same RC2 ISO BIOS boot passed with CPU qemu64 and normal multi-thread TCG, without icount. Latest completed real Web/warm-reboot/backup-PD checks use this configuration; further lifecycle remains separate. Distributed basic launcher does not force CPU max.
limits: Observed environment comparison, not a diagnosis of QEMU internals or a general hardware-boot guarantee; actual final lifecycle results are recorded separately.
